lessons.title: Select only the rows you need
lessons.body:
### Start with a question
SELECT chooses columns. FROM names the source. WHERE filters rows before aggregation. ORDER BY chooses the output order.

```sql
SELECT product, amount
FROM exercise_sales
WHERE amount >= 40
ORDER BY amount DESC;
```

Use IS NULL to test for missing values. Comparing a value with NULL using = does not produce an ordinary true result.

lessons.title: GROUP BY & HAVING
lessons.body:
### Turn rows into groups
GROUP BY combines rows by a grouping key. Aggregates such as SUM and COUNT compute a value for each group. WHERE filters input rows; HAVING filters aggregated groups.

Select grouped columns and aggregates deliberately. Avoid relying on SQLite’s permissive handling of ungrouped columns when writing queries intended for other engines.

### Check the result
Always decide whether the count represents all rows, non-null values, or distinct values.

exercises.title: Summarize sales by category
exercises.prompt: Return category, item count as items, and total amount as total. Include only categories with total at least 120. Sort by total descending. Load the exercise dataset before running the query.
exercises.answer:
```sql
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS items, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM exercise_sales
GROUP BY category
HAVING SUM(amount) >= 120
ORDER BY total DESC;
```
